about: The Nada family has farmed the steep hills of Treiso, one of the villages of the Barbaresco zone, since 1900, when an ancestor bought a vineyard, an orchard and a small house in the Casot cru. Local history has it the seller was a man named Gaja. The family began bottling its own wine in 1964, before Barbaresco even had its DOC, and dug a cellar into the hill beneath the house in 1968. Giuseppe and Nella Nada still work the vines; their daughter Barbara runs the business and their son Enrico, a trained enologist, makes the wine.

Casot is the estate’s flagship: about 3.5 hectares of southwest-facing Nebbiolo at around 350 metres, on calcareous marl, with vines planted between 1960 and 2012. The family converted to organic farming in 2014, with certification from 2017. Enrico lets the grapes ferment spontaneously in stainless steel, then gives them a long maceration on the skins, about 65 days in recent vintages. The wine ages for two years in large, old casks before six months in bottle.

This is traditional Barbaresco, built for both early pleasure and long aging: dark red fruit set against spice, flowers and balsamic notes, with fine, elegant tannins and a long finish. Importer Bowler Wine describes the Nada wines as having “a transparent nonchalance in the glass.” The family’s Casot wines have a track record of aging gracefully for two decades or more, though they are already open and generous in their youth.
facts: Casot cru, Treiso; southwest-facing, about 350 m, calcareous marl
Spontaneous, in stainless steel, with extended maceration
About 2 years in large old casks, then bottle
